title: Head of Audit for Human Resources, Legal, Organizational Behavior and Legal Entity Audit, MD
description: Head of Audit for Human Resources, Legal, Organizational Behavior and Legal Entity Audit – Managing Director Who we are looking for In this role, you will lead Corporate Audit’s global portfolio covering Human Resources, Legal, Global Security, ESG, Regulatory Liaison, Workplace Conduct, Investigations and Organizational Behavior, together with audit coverage of the India legal entity and hub location. You will report directly to the Global Head of Audit for HR, Legal, Finance, Custody and the Asia region, and lead a team of audit professionals across the United States and India. You will set the coverage approach across the portfolio, establish Corporate Audit’s enterprise-wide framework to audit organizational behavior, and strengthen how investigation and speak-up matters referred to Corporate Audit translate into control improvements. The role will be based in Boston, MA or New Jersey and may be performed in a hybrid model, with expectation to be in office 4 days per week. Key responsibilities of this role include: Lead Portfolio Audit Coverage: Develop, own and execute a risk-based global assurance plan and coverage approach across the portfolio, responsive to emerging risks and regulatory developments. Establish Organizational Behavior Auditing: Build, operationalize and embed an enterprise-wide approach for auditing organizational behavior, supported by methodology and risk indicators. Strengthen Investigation Outcomes: Enhance Corporate Audit’s handling of speak-up and investigation referrals so that conclusions address underlying control and process gaps, with remediation tracked to closure. Provide Legal Entity Assurance: Lead audit coverage of the hub location and support legal entity governance and Board reporting. Lead Teams and Influence Stakeholders: Build a high-performing global team and engage senior management, governance committees and regulators to drive sustainable improvements. Why this role is important to us The team you will be joining plays a critical role in the overall success of the organization. The portfolio covers risks that shape our people, conduct, legal and control environment, including our India hub, which is home to a significant part of our workforce. Institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges and drive performance, and our regulators and Board rely on Corporate Audit for independent assurance that these risks are well governed. Join us if you are ready to shape how internal audit addresses behavioral and conduct risk in a global financial institution. What you will be responsible for As Head of Human Resources, Legal, Security, Organizational Behavior and Legal Entity Audit, you will: Drive the development and execution of a risk-based audit plan for the portfolio through risk assessments that consider existing and emerging risks, strategic initiatives, regulatory expectations and the effectiveness of the control environment. Lead the design, implementation and continued evolution of Corporate Audit’s Organizational Behavior audit framework, methodology and risk indicators, in line with Institute of Internal Auditors requirements, and deploy it across standalone, thematic and integrated audit coverage. Build the behavioral risk knowledge, skills and capability maturity of the entire audit function to cover organizational behavior risks, and represent the third line on this topic across State Street. Strengthen and further formalize Corporate Audit’s review of speak-up and whistleblower matters, ensuring conclusions extend beyond individual conduct to identify contributing control or process gaps, and that resulting actions are tracked, validated and closed. Lead audit coverage of the India legal entity, including delivery of risk-based audits, supporting Legal Entity Board reporting, including views on regulatory compliance. Review, approve and communicate audit deliverables, including findings, memos, reports and thematic insights, to senior and executive management and governance committees. Influence effective and sustainable improvements to processes and controls through insights gained from risk and control expertise. Participate as a non-voting member of steering committees and management working groups, promoting balanced discussion and encouraging challenges and debate. Provide insight into the evolving regulatory environment and interact with global and local regulators. Develop and maintain stakeholder relationships across the portfolio, increasing risk insight and awareness. Build, lead and develop a global team, including talent management, hiring and succession planning. What we value These skills will help you succeed in this role: Excellent analytical, written communication, interpersonal, organizational and presentation skills, including communicating with Boards, committees and regulators. Sound risk and control judgment, professional skepticism and the confidence to challenge constructively at senior levels.

title: Senior Manager, Provisioning
description: Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence. This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk. We are seeking an experienced, strategic, and operational leader to join our Order-to-Cash (O2C) organization as the Senior Manager, Provisioning . In this role, you will define the operational vision, long-term roadmap, and fulfillment standards for our global provisioning function. You will lead a global team responsible for the timely, accurate execution of SaaS tenant activations, contract adjustments, and license fulfillments across all enterprise product lines. You will serve as the primary operational escalation point for executive leadership, technical support, and customers regarding fulfillment and order activation and deactivation while partnering closely with Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, and Business Technology. Key Responsibilities 1. Strategic & Operational Leadership Define Function Strategy: Establish and execute the operational roadmap, capacity models, and service-level agreements (SLAs) for global provisioning in alignment with Order-to-Cash (O2C) objectives. Operational Excellence: Maintain rigorous queue governance, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and quality controls to drive high accuracy and throughput across all fulfillment queues. Systems & Process Automation: Partner with Business Technology and Engineering teams to prioritize automation initiatives, API integrations, and system enhancements that reduce manual touchpoints. 2. Escalations & Stakeholder Management Leadership & Customer Escalations: Serve as the senior escalation point for urgent fulfillment requests, deprovisioning escalations, complex contract structures, technical support blockers, and direct enterprise customer inquiries. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, and Billing to streamline order handoffs, validate non-standard contractual terms, and resolve operational blockers prior to fulfillment. Executive Reporting: Provide regular operational readouts, KPI scorecards, and performance trends to senior leadership. 3. Compliance, Audit & Quality Governance Reconciliation & Integrity: Create and oversee regular reconciliation between CRM/ERP systems (Salesforce, NetSuite) and production fulfillment environments to ensure contract and tenant alignment. Audit & SOX Readiness: Enforce strict adherence to internal controls, SOX requirements, and SOC compliance frameworks for all provisioning operations. Specialized Compliance Standards: Support operational requirements for public sector and regulated environments (e.g., FedRAMP fulfillment protocols). 4. Team Building & Talent Development People Leadership: Lead, coach, and scale a high-performing, globally distributed operational team, cultivating a culture of accountability, precision, and operational ownership. Talent Enablement: Build structured onboarding programs, competency frameworks, and clear career development paths to develop and retain talent. Resource Management: Optimize global shift models and resource allocation to ensure resilient, continuous fulfillment coverage. Qualifications Experience: 8+ years of progressive experience in Provisioning, Support, Deal Operations, Sales Operations, or Order-to-Cash within an enterprise SaaS environment with a minimum of 4 in provisioning. People Management: 4+ years of direct people-management experience leading and developing global or multi-site operational teams. Domain Knowledge: In-depth understanding of the Quote-to-Cash (Q2C) lifecycle, SaaS subscription mechanics, and order-to-provisioning workflows. Systems Proficiency: Hands-on experience with enterprise tools including Salesforce CPQ, NetSuite, and workflow/ticketing platforms (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow, or SFDC cases). Compliance & Controls: Practical knowledge of SOX compliance, order verification controls, and audit processes. Executive Presence: Strong communication and problem-solving skills with demonstrated experience managing high-visibility escalations with customers and senior leaders. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Information Systems, Finance, or equivalent practical experience in addition to 8 above. title: Lead Analyst, Financial Crimes
description: About the role Chime's Financial Crimes team protects millions of members from money laundering, fraud, and the organized networks that target consumer financial platforms. We work in a bank-partner model: we run detection and investigation, and we escalate unusual activity to our bank partners, who hold the filing obligation. That means our written work product is read by outside parties, and the quality bar is correspondingly high. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will set the standard for how financial crime work is done here rather than working a queue — defining what good looks like, raising the ceiling for the analysts you lead, and owning the hardest problems on the team end to end. In this role, you can expect to Operate with minimal direction on problems that arrive ambiguous, and you define the approach rather than waiting for one. Set the quality standard others calibrate to with defensible judgement calls. Move work across team boundaries without formal authority, and you are trusted to represent Financial Crimes to partners outside the function. Raise the ceiling of the people around you — through calibration, coaching, documentation, and the examples you set in your own casework. Improve the system, not just the case. Every hard investigation should leave behind something reusable: a control, a procedure, a detection change, or a documented typology. What you will own: Vendor Management. You will lead, and support, a team of analysts. Vendor team quality. You sample operations work, run calibration with partners, keep apprised of quality assurance trends, and hold quality and productivity expectations where they belong. Risk trend analysis. You understand AML and Fraud risks well enough to follow the pattern of unusual activity across accounts, devices, funding sources, counterparties, and behavioral patterns, and you can show the shape of a network in a way a non-investigator understands. Typology development. You document new and evolving schemes, make them teachable to the wider team, identify if opportunities in coverage are needed, and own the creation of coverage with partners as appropriate. Operational rollout of new coverage. When a new typology or scenario goes live, you design how it will be worked — routing, procedure, evidence standard, and quality checks — before the first alert lands. Procedures and documentation. You own the SOPs for your area and keep them in a state where a third party could read them cold and understand what we do and why. Audit and exam readiness. You prepare the operational side for internal audit, independent testing, and bank partner reviews, and you own remediation of findings assigned to operations through to closure. To thrive in this role, you have 7+ years in financial crime, fraud, or risk investigations at a bank, fintech, payments company, or comparable regulated environment. Working command of BSA, the USA PATRIOT Act, OFAC requirements, and unusual/suspicious activity reporting standards — enough to explain not just the rule but why it exists. Deep experience across the transaction monitoring alert lifecycle at real volume, including the operational tradeoffs that come with it. Real typology depth across both money laundering and fraud — mule and money movement networks, first-party fraud, synthetic and stolen identity, scams and social engineering, elder financial exploitation, etc. Hands-on involvement in scenario tuning or threshold work alongside data or risk partners, with an understanding of what changing a threshold actually costs. Experience overseeing vendor or outsourced investigation teams. Judgment under volume. You can distinguish the case that deserves forty hours from the one that deserves forty minutes.   Comfort with sustained ambiguity. You will spend real time on hypotheses that do not pan out, and you need the judgment to know when to stop. Advanced SQL, and fluency with graph or link analysis tooling for mapping relationships at scale. CAMS, CFE, or equivalent certification preferred. #LI-Onsite #LI-BE1 Below is the base salary offered for this role and level of experience. Full-time employees may also be eligible for bonus(es), competitive equity, and benefits. For commissioned roles, the base salary listed in this job description does not include incentive/variable pay. The actual base salary offered may be higher, depending on your location, skills, qualifications, and experience. Through our user-friendly tools and intuitive platforms, we empower our members to take control of their finances and work towards their goals.
